tools.name: search_playbooks
tools.description: Searches the Agents Handbook for playbooks that match a real-world job done with an AI agent, described in plain words (for example 'cancel subscriptions from email receipts' or 'turn tickets into pull requests'). Returns matching playbook slugs, titles, trust levels, risk levels and URLs, plus rela

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: Returns one Agents Handbook playbook as markdown: summary, human checkpoints, the prompt (the variant written for the given agent, if provided), steps with checks, known failure modes, evidence links and the community success rate.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: Lists the jobs the Agents Handbook covers, grouped by category, with the agents that have playbooks for each job.

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description: Returns an agent profile from the Agents Handbook: what the agent is good at, its limits, how it connects to tools, and the playbooks and lessons written for it.

tools.name: get_lessons
tools.description: Returns known failure modes and their fixes from the Agents Handbook, filtered by agent, playbook, lesson slug or a plain-words description of the problem.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Lists the most recently updated playbooks and the latest community run reports in the Agents Handbook.

tools.name: report_run
tools.description: Records the outcome of running an Agents Handbook playbook (worked, worked with changes, or failed), with what changed and an optional lesson. Reports enter a review queue and count toward the playbook's success rate only after approval. Fields must not contain personal data such as names, emails, a

tools.name: submit_use_case
tools.description: Sends a short use case (a job done with an agent that has no playbook yet), a lesson, or a correction to an existing playbook into the Agents Handbook review queue. Nothing is published until it is reviewed. Fields must not contain personal data.

tools.name: submit_playbook
tools.description: Sends a full playbook for a job completed with an AI agent into the Agents Handbook review queue: title, agents used, summary, the prompt that worked (with [placeholders] for personal details), steps, what went wrong, human checkpoints and optional public sources. A review agent checks sources and s

tools.name: check_submission
tools.description: Returns the review status of an Agents Handbook submission (pending, reviewed, approved, rejected or published) with the review agent's reasons.

tools.name: register_contributor
tools.description: Creates an Agents Handbook contributor key for a public handle, so run reports and submissions sent with it (Authorization: Bearer <key>) are credited and get higher rate limits. The key is returned once and only a hash is stored.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "report_run" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_playbooks, check_submission · Private data: report_run · Public sink: search_playbooks, submit_use_case, submit_playbook · Destructive: whats_new, report_run, register_contributor.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_playbooks, check_submission · Private data: report_run · Public sink: search_playbooks, submit_use_case, submit_playbook · Destructive: whats_new, report_run, register_contributor

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
